title: DocBook
tagline: A personal library of long-form technical books.

books.title: Systems Programming & Software Architecture Foundations with C++
books.subtitle: An architecture-first, runtime-first guide using C++ as the teaching language
books.description: For intermediate developers who can write code but want to understand what is actually happening when their code runs — and why software is built the way it is.

parts.title: Part 1 — What Programming Actually Is
parts.summary: The substrate. How programs become processes, what the CPU and memory really are, what the OS does on your behalf, and how source code becomes machine code. By the end you have an unbroken mental model from the program counter up to source code.

chapters.title: What Happens When A Program Runs
chapters.subtitle: The kernel, loader, dynamic linker, and C runtime — the four actors that all run before your main()

chapters.title: CPU, RAM, Stack, Heap, Registers
chapters.subtitle: Fetch–decode–execute. Why memory is a hierarchy, not a single thing

chapters.title: How Operating Systems Execute Programs
chapters.subtitle: Processes, virtual memory, syscalls, scheduling, and the four core OS abstractions

chapters.title: Machine Code, Assembly, Compilers, Interpreters
chapters.subtitle: From source to bytes. Why every language has a runtime if you look hard enough

chapters.title: Memory Layout Of A Process
chapters.subtitle: .text, .rodata, .data, .bss, heap, stack, libraries, TLS — where every variable lives

chapters.title: Function Calls Internally
chapters.subtitle: Calling conventions, stack frames, register saving, inlining, tail calls

chapters.title: Call Stack Deep Dive
chapters.subtitle: Stack traces, debugger walking, overflow, and the trick behind coroutines, fibers, and exceptions

chapters.title: Pointers As Memory Addresses
chapters.subtitle: Typed views of addresses. Pointers, references, smart pointers, and why every language has hidden pointers

chapters.title: Why Abstractions Exist
chapters.subtitle: Contracts that separate what from how. Why we cannot skip them; what they always cost

chapters.title: What Languages Actually Do
chapters.subtitle: Languages as bundles of design decisions. The axes every language sits on

parts.title: Part 2 — Memory & Execution Foundations
parts.summary: The dimension that dominates real-world performance and reliability. Stack and heap internals, manual memory management, ownership, lifetimes, RAII, fragmentation, the cache hierarchy, data-oriented design, smart pointers, reference counting, garbage collection, and how Python/Go/PHP runtimes actually manage memory.

chapters.title: Stack vs Heap Internals
chapters.subtitle: Two disciplines, not two places. Stack frames, malloc internals, thread-local arenas

chapters.title: Manual Memory Management
chapters.subtitle: malloc/new/placement new/alignment, the four bug families, sanitizers

chapters.title: Ownership Models
chapters.subtitle: Five patterns across C, C++, Rust, and GC'd languages. Move semantics concretely

chapters.title: Lifetimes
chapters.subtitle: Storage duration vs object lifetime. Temporaries, lifetime extension, dangling refs

chapters.title: RAII Explained Deeply
chapters.subtitle: Constructor acquires, destructor releases. Stack unwinding. Rule of Zero/Three/Five

chapters.title: Memory Fragmentation
chapters.subtitle: Internal vs external. Why long-running services drift. Pools and arenas

chapters.title: Caches and CPU Locality
chapters.subtitle: The memory hierarchy. Cache lines, prefetchers, why std::list is wrong

chapters.title: Data-Oriented Design
chapters.subtitle: AoS vs SoA. ECS pattern. Hot/cold splitting. SIMD-friendly layouts

chapters.title: Smart Pointers Internals
chapters.subtitle: unique_ptr, shared_ptr control blocks, weak_ptr, make_shared, atomic cost

chapters.title: Reference Counting
chapters.subtitle: Atomic vs non-atomic counts. Cycles. CPython, Swift ARC, ObjC ARC

chapters.title: Garbage Collection Internals
chapters.subtitle: Mark-sweep, copying, generational, tri-color, concurrent collectors. JVM, Go, V8

chapters.title: How Python, Go, and PHP Actually Manage Memory
chapters.subtitle: Four runtimes side by side. Implications and common per-language mistakes

parts.title: Part 3 — Understanding Abstractions
parts.summary: Abstractions, taken apart mechanically. What an abstraction is built out of, encapsulation from first principles, what classes and objects are in memory, composition vs inheritance, interfaces and contracts, polymorphism internals, virtual tables, static vs dynamic dispatch, and dependency injection from scratch.
